title: Walnut key rack with hooks
subtitle: Seasoned wood: a wall-hung key rack planed and routed from walnut, with brass cup hooks
excerpt: A wall-mounted key rack in dark walnut: a single planed board with a routed edge profile and five brass cup hooks screwed underneath. The board is finished with raw linseed oil to show the walnut grain. Hanging with a recessed slot on the back, no visible fixings on the face.
sourceNotes: Cassell's Cyclopaedia of Mechanics vol. III (1885) for the planed board and recessed slot hanging method; Newey & Drage Practical Carpentry for the linseed oil finishing protocol.

glossaryTerms.definition: The slot or cut made by a saw blade through wood.
A small screw hook with a cupped shape at the end, traditionally used for hanging cups and keys.

content.text: A walnut key rack is a planed board with hooks screwed underneath: simple in construction but rewarding when made from a piece of timber worth showing. Walnut is chosen for its dark colour and contrast with brass cup hooks; the grain planes without difficulty and oil finish brings out the figure. The hanging system is a recessed slot on the back that locates on a single wall screw: no visible fixings on the face.
What you need
Wood

One seasoned walnut board, 45 cm long, 8 cm wide, 18 mm thick. Black walnut (Juglans nigra) from a timber supplier or English walnut (Juglans regia), the colour and figure are similar. Avoid walnut with wild grain (a curly figure is attractive but planes against the grain on every pass).
Tools
No. 5 hand plane for face preparation.
Tenon saw for the recessed slot.
Combination square and marking gauge.
Cordless drill for pilot holes for the cup hooks.
Sandpaper 120 and 240 grit.
Five brass cup hooks.
Raw linseed oil.
The work
Step 1: Plane the face

Secure the board face-up in a vice. Plane with the grain to produce a flat surface with no wind (twist). Walnut planes cleanly if the iron is sharp; a dull iron leaves a burnished surface that takes oil unevenly. Finish the face with a light smoothing pass and sand to 240 grit.
Step 2: Cut the recessed hanging slot
On the back of the board, use the tenon saw to cut a
kerf

at 45 degrees along the top edge, 6 mm from the top face, cutting across the full width of the board. Deepen this kerf to 8 mm with two saw passes. When the board is placed over a wall screw, the screw head drops into this slot and the board rests on the screw shaft, the 45-degree angle prevents it from coming forward off the screw.
Step 3: Mark and fit the cup hooks
Mark five hook positions on the bottom face of the board, evenly spaced 8 cm apart, 15 mm from the lower edge. Drill a pilot hole at each mark to prevent the walnut from splitting when the
cup hooks
are screwed in. Screw each hook by hand.
Finishing

Apply one coat of raw linseed oil to all surfaces by hand. Leave to soak for 30 minutes, then wipe off the excess. Cure for two weeks before hanging in a dry position. RLO rags: lay flat to dry, never crumple. Raw linseed oil on walnut produces a warm honey tone that deepens over time.

attrs.symptom: The board rocks on the wall after hanging, the slot does not sit flat against the wall
attrs.cause: The slot cut angle is too steep or too shallow, so the board does not sit flush
attrs.fix: Recut the slot with the saw at a steeper angle (closer to 45 degrees) to allow the board to sit with its back face flat against the wall. The slot geometry is critical, the 45-degree angle is what keeps the board from tilting.
